head: Records involving Anthropic’s network cover 452 of 533 members of Congress.
deck: One seat per member serving on Nov. 26, 2026. The network includes Anthropic, its funders, funded groups, and their PACs and lobbyists.
note: Outside activity includes spending against a member. The records can’t establish an effect on a vote.
bridge: Start with campaign gifts from Anthropic’s employees and its PAC.
source: FEC, lobbying and other public records · Congress pack

head: Gifts from Anthropic employees and its PAC reached 199 sitting members, up from 10.
deck: Lit seats mark gifts to linked committees. Both chambers use the Nov. 26, 2026 roster.
note: The gifts are employees’ own money or the PAC’s money. Employers are as filed. A gift can’t tell us how someone voted.
bridge: Anthropic also announced money for a political nonprofit.

head: Anthropic announced $40.0M for Public First Action in 2026.
deck: Public First Action is a political nonprofit.
note: The filings collected here leave the nonprofit’s donors undisclosed and trace no contribution to a specific expenditure.
bridge: Campaign money is one record. Which bills did lobbying reports filed for Anthropic name?
source: Anthropic’s own announcements · Public First Action

head: Chip proposals led the stand-alone bills named in reports filed for Anthropic.
deck: 18 of 68 reports named a bill. Jan. 2023–Sept. 2026.
note: Paired House and Senate versions count together. A bill mention leaves Anthropic’s position open.
bridge: How much of the wider federal lobbying field did the network account for?
source: Federal lobbying reports and Congress.gov bill records

head: Anthropic’s network reported 0.5% of 2025 federal lobbying dollars on filings naming AI.
deck: Each client’s total covers all issues on those reports.
note: These figures put an upper bound on AI lobbying. Client matching and expense coverage are provisional.
bridge: Another comparison runs in the opposite direction, from political offices and committees to the labs.

head: These spending records show 2.3 times as much paid to OpenAI as to Anthropic.
deck: Political committees and House offices paid the labs.
note: These are purchases. The search covered a subset of committees, and card descriptions may bundle charges.
bridge: What happens when different records count toward the same total?

head: Ted Lieu and Thom Tillis counted equally.
deck: Each occupies one seat in the tally of members named in records involving Anthropic’s network.
note: The records don’t say what any of this did to a vote.
source: Congress pack member records · FEC reports
